pageProps.title: The Sleeping Forest
pageProps.review: An early work in Keigo Higashino's Detective Kyoichiro Kaga series, this review introduces the charm of a romantic mystery novel that uncovers the truth while deeply insighting the motives for crime and human desires set in a closed ballet society.
pageProps.description: A brilliant tragedy created by devoted love
pageProps.content:
## Review An important early work that determined the direction of Detective Kyoichiro Kaga, who occupies a significant weight in the author's worldview. It is said to be a monumental work where he first appears as a professional detective belonging to the Metropolitan Police Department.
Detective Kaga focuses on why, the motive for the crime, rather than ```how```, the method of the crime. An investigation method based on empathy and psychological insight is said to be his symbolic feature that also appears in subsequent series.
Should I call it a ```romantic mystery```? This work can be said to be a somewhat complex work where romance, mystery, and human desire are intricately mixed.
A unique situation is created where the detective's personal emotional involvement becomes a weakness in solving the case and simultaneously an essential tool for uncovering the truth.
The world of ```ballet``` is depicted as a microcosm of a competitive closed society where extreme psychological pressure, eating disorders, and cruel competition are hidden under the names of physical perfection and artistic expression. This closely links the background of the case with the theme.
